Cα(T) = min{L(T), Qα(T)}.
For δ > 0, a terminal crisis occurs when Cα(T) ≥δ. Thus the mean loss and at least k individual
losses must each reach δ. The target is selected independently of the price-response function.
The discrete coverage rule is material: for N = 3, α = 0.9 means k = 3, so it requires a fall in all
three assets. More generally, the contrast k = N versus k < N determines whether a compensating
asset exists at all. This same distinction appears first in the A/B/C classification and later in the
multiday cross-asset capacity inequality. A first-passage event τα,δ = inf{t : Cα(t) ≥δ} is different
from a terminal crisis under dollar closure; we study the latter.
